nodes.label: Live Widgets and Controls
nodes.rationale: Every widget is live: tapping a lamp, scene or AC switches it without opening the app, on the Home Screen, Lock Screen, StandBy, Control Center and the Mac desktop.

nodes.label: HomeSnapshot
nodes.rationale: Rooms, lamps, ACs, furniture footprints and scenes with their state are posted after every change, so a widget can draw the home without the app or the network.

nodes.label: App Group home.json with flock
nodes.rationale: The snapshot and action queue live in the App Group container and are read and written under one flock, so the app and a widget never see half of each other's work.

nodes.label: App Intent Tap Handling
nodes.rationale: A tap applies the change to the snapshot with the same rules as the panel's store (scenes, clamping, 'a white temperature drops the colour'), so the widget redraws with the result at once while the real command is queued.

nodes.label: Darwin Notification Wake-Up
nodes.rationale: A Darwin notification wakes the running Mac app so it takes the queue within milliseconds instead of polling.

nodes.label: Mac Widget Action Path
nodes.rationale: The app runs in the menu bar and runs each queued action through the panel, the same path as a click, so it reaches Smart Life, Home Assistant, Hue and the island, and the widget redraws with the real outcome.

nodes.label: iPhone Widget Direct-to-Platform Path
nodes.rationale: The iPhone app is usually not running, so the extension sends the change itself to Home Assistant, Hue and Smart Life using Keychain-group connections; Apple Home actions wait in the queue for the app to open.

nodes.label: Queued Action Expires After Ten Minutes
nodes.rationale: Nobody expects a lamp to switch an hour later, and an action is only ever run for the home it was made in, so a stale queue cannot act on a different home.

nodes.label: Controls and Quick Actions
nodes.rationale: iOS 18 / macOS 26 controls (All Lights, Light, Scene, Air Conditioner) and icon quick actions put the common switches on the Lock Screen, Action button and long-press menu.

nodes.label: Widget Signing and App Group Identifiers
nodes.rationale: The Mac uses a team-prefixed group so no provisioning profile is needed, and an ad-hoc release has no team so the group is the bare identifier; whether a sandboxed ad-hoc widget can read it is untested, hence the advice to build with a free Apple Development certificate.

nodes.label: render-widgets Still Renderer
nodes.rationale: Renders PNGs of every widget without WidgetKit, so widget design can be reviewed and screenshotted outside Xcode.
